reason: Confirmed in-scope claim c1: the kernel's tower-field S-box math is wrong for essentially every byte. A full 256-byte sweep (probe t9) against an independently computed FIPS 197 S-box found 255/256 mismatched values under exact byte comparison, including the contract's explicitly stated check pairs — x=0 yields 108 instead of 0x63 and x=0x53 yields 85 instead of 0xed. The contract (problem.txt) requires the exact specified value at every position with no numerical tolerance for every byte 0..255 in any legal input, so this is a direct violation of an explicitly required behavior. Secondary concerns (c2 view handling/aliasing, c3 tail masking at non-multiple-of-256 lengths) were isolated via probes t10/t16: input backing storage is preserved, output is fresh non-aliasing contiguous, and outputs conform position-wise to the kernel's own byte map at all edge lengths with surrounding bytes untouched — no defect beyond the global math error. Those claims remain inconclusive/not material to the verdict. Skeptic reviewed the latest evidence (t17) and recorded no new claims.
